concepts.def: Base-16, a shorthand for binary (0–9, A–F).
A bit is one binary digit; 8 bits make a byte.
ASCII and Unicode represent text as binary codes.
Images stored as pixels with a colour depth.
Sound sampled at a rate and bit depth to store digitally.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Data Representation — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Data Representation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Data Representation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In 8-bit two's complement representation, a leading 1 indicates that the number is:
options: Even
Prime
Negative
Greater than 127
Can represent characters from far more of the world's writing systems
Uses fewer bits for every character
Can only encode English letters
Is restricted to 128 characters

mcqs.q: The colour depth of a bitmap image is:
options: The number of pixels in the image
The physical size of the screen
The number of bits used to represent each pixel
The brightness of the display

mcqs.q: What is the range of integers an 8-bit two's complement number can store?
options: -128 to +127: the leading bit carries weight -128, so the negative side reaches one further than the positive side.
0 to 255, the same as an unsigned byte.
-127 to +127, because the range must be symmetrical around zero.
No - colour depth has no effect on the number of colours.

mcqs.q: What comes after F when counting in hexadecimal?
options: No - colour depth has no effect on the number of colours.
G - the alphabet simply continues after F.
F1 - you append a 1 to the F.
10 (one-zero), which represents denary 16; the digits restart and a new place value column begins, just as 9 rolls over to 10 in denary.

mcqs.q: Does doubling the colour depth of an image double the number of available colours?
options: F1 - you append a 1 to the F.
Yes - twice the bits means twice the colours.
No - each extra BIT doubles the colours, so going from 8-bit to 16-bit multiplies the available colours by 2^8 = 256, not by 2.
No - colour depth has no effect on the number of colours.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Binary”?
options: The base-2 number system using only digits 0 and 1, in which each place value is double the one to its right.
A way of representing signed integers in which the most significant bit carries a negative weight, allowing subtraction via addition.
Converting analogue sound to digital data by measuring the wave's amplitude at regular intervals; the sample rate is measurements per second.
An image stored as a grid of pixels, where resolution is the number of pixels and colour depth is the bits used per pixel.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Character encoding”?
options: A mapping from characters to binary codes; ASCII uses 7 bits while Unicode can represent characters from virtually all writing systems.
The base-2 number system using only digits 0 and 1, in which each place value is double the one to its right.
An image stored as a grid of pixels, where resolution is the number of pixels and colour depth is the bits used per pixel.
The base-16 number system using digits 0-9 and letters A-F, often used as a compact, human-friendly shorthand for binary values.
